pr_title: Show error and warning indicators in project panel items
pr_body:
Closes #5016

Release Notes:

- Add setting to display error and warning indicators in project panel items.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f8031e6-ca47-42bf-a7eb-718eb1067f36
pr_comments:
Okay I played around a little bit and I have a concrete suggestion:
Let's add a `"show_diagnostic_errors"` bool property in the `"project_panel"` object in the `settings.json`. I would use a default value of `true`, but happy to make it `false` if you like it better. 

I would not show warnings in the project panel. I think this causes too much unnecessary noise. The status `GitFileStatus::Modified` paints the items with the color `Color::Modified` which is very similar to `Color::Warning` (at least in the theme `One Light`) and this is very confusing.

If people want to display warnings as well, I am happy to make a follow-up PR but I honestly do not think someone wants this.

I will implement this and add the docs next week if you think this would be a good add.

I implemented it the way I suggested in the last comment. Looking forward to your feedback on this!

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fe4465d-afbb-4edb-abfe-e7d33991b0a5
@mrnugget can you please take a look at this PR ? Tagging you because of the time zone^^
cc @danilo-leal in case you have thoughts wrt to design

> If people want to display warnings as well, I am happy to make a follow-up PR but I honestly do not think someone wants this.\

I'd like to have this and would prefer to add this in this PR as well, so that we do not have to break the settings right after this is released.
Maybe we could have a setting like (not sure about the names of the enum variants):
`"show_diagnostics": "off/all/errors"`

> I would not show warnings in the project panel. I think this causes too much unnecessary noise. The status GitFileStatus::Modified paints the items with the color Color::Modified which is very similar to Color::Warning (at least in the theme One Light) and this is very confusing.

Let's add the warnings as an option and we will figure out how to make it "pretty" later.

Hey so this is how it looks like with warnings and the settings as @bennetbo suggested:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d866e25-b65c-4304-ba38-f6e0fcf0170f

PS: I changed my GPG key last night and apparently you should not remove the old public key from your profile, otherwise old commits show up as unverified. It's still me, just wiser.

One thing that I'm now wondering about: how will a modified file look different from a file with warnings? Right now, modified files look like this: 
![screenshot-2024-09-25-10 15 52@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa1b752c-4ca9-469f-8337-0bf069a14b0d)

That's also the has-a-warning style, no?

I'd avoid using only colors for these statuses—different themes will have different color qualities, and relying only on them can be very tricky. We can't guarantee that it will look great in all themes, and folks with any visual impairments can have an even harder time! 

That said, I'd consider adding the same icons we display on the status bar for errors and warnings and simple dot indicators for the Git-related statuses (added & modified) to the project item. I'd also add tooltips to them.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d52ac53e-9f55-42f6-878f-80d3bbda81dd)
Thank you for working on this! It's the only thing keeping me from using Zed as my main editor at this point. 🙂

Hey @nilskch! Thanks for contributing. 

I'm looking into some design considerations around this today, I'll come back and add more detail shortly – just adding a quick note so you aren't waiting around with no feedback.
@iamnbutler sounds good to me, thanks!

This is how @danilo-leal 's suggestion looks like (I like it!): And just for fun without the dots for a git status: This theme is `Gruvbox Dark` and I think in this theme `Color::Warning` and `Color::Modified` are exactly the same. EDIT: I centered the icons. What do you think?
personly, I like the icon ends with alignment.
@CharlesChen0823 very nice idea!

I think the dots in addition are a bit much, but with only the icons, I'd say we can merge this.

(If you want: I'd be interested to see what it would look like if the opacity of the icons color is turned to 70% if they are warning/error colored, because those red folders really stick out)

I agree with the dots. I change the opacity to 70% this evening (CET) and see how it looks like :)

Also happy to implement anything that @iamnbutler proposes!

What do you think about the settings? They are hard to change once we merge and we should get them right. Theoretically there are more diagnostic severities (`INFORMATION` and `HINT` and maybe more in the future?) and I think we should design the settings in a way that they are extendable. Also, the current design doesn't allow for just showing warnings and not errors (I do not want this but still wanted to mention it). We could add an extra enum variant for that but the number of variants would explode with the number of severity types if you want to support every combination.

What if the dots are placed right after (or even on the left side of) the file name and only the icons at the right edge? To me they are two very orthogonal features and I think I'd want to have both most of the time.
@mrnugget 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, and 1.0

Hey @nilskch, thanks so much for the continued work here! Just to give you an update, @iamnbutler & I have looked into this change yesterday and tried to figure out the design taking into consideration other project panel-related changes going on at the moment (particularly horizontal scrolling) that would affect what we're doing here as those add new complexities. So, the approach we came up with that we've enjoyed the most was this one: Visually speaking, it's very different than what we're playing with here, but it has some pros. It works with horizontal scrolling and doesn't overloads the project panel items with too many colors—we want to be conscious about the growing visual complexity in Zed. It also might have some yet unanswered questions, like: - How do we display, on a folder, that there's a file with diagnostic inside it? (The `cloudflare` example directory in the picture doesn't feel like the best solution yet) - How do we move on with this approach if file icons are disabled? Maybe what we have in the second picture suffices? Or would it be confusing because of how an X icon could be confused with a close action? That said, we might take a bit more time to go through these, before pushing through this PR, and then give an update here with clearer designs. We might also discuss horizontal scrolling and its implications in taking on this convo! Thanks for bearing with us 😊

Hey, thanks for taking the time on this! I completely understand your points. This feature is quite important to me (and I think for most other VS Code transitioners as well), so I am happy to spend more time on this to make it happen. Feel free to use me as a resource to implement different designs to figure out what works best!

If you can post a video it would be appreciated.

P.s.
This system also works with other languages, for example js.

Hey, I totally agree with @WeetHet, the design looks great! I dont know what the status on horizontal scrolling is, but do you have any new design ideas? Or can I implement your solution?

Amazing work! Just a couple of small nitpicks:
- Maybe make the icons a bit smaller so they don't overlap with the file icons that much, especially, when folder icons are disabled
- When the file icons are disabled, I would prefer for the files to still be aligned, so maybe move the files with the errors a bit to the right, as it is done in the original proposal

Forgot to record folder icons with warnings...

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/647ba041-9988-4f2e-8438-efd2b8afd940

> When the file icons are disabled, I would prefer for the files to still be aligned, so maybe move the files with the errors a bit to the right, as it is done in the original proposal

Not sure what you mean, I just swap the file icon (or the empty placeholder of the file icon) with an X or a triangle. Can you explain this a little more?

I'd propose to replace the current behaviour with `"file_icons": "empty"` and add a `"file_icons": "none"` option that would completely get rid of that space. If a file has errors of warnings, it would move that file to the right and add a respective icon on the left. That behaviour matches @danilo-leal's renders a bit better, and in my mind looks better too

Also, it seems like in the renders, the opened folders don't have an indicator. I might only imagine it's intentional, as you can see the error below anyways, and an angle icon with a cross pointing down doesn't really look great

@nilskch : Great work, some considerations: Taking inspiration from the image of @danilo-leal in detail: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dba342ae-30ed-4ac4-86da-577002c4d419) 1) When folder icon is false, then you can see that the arrow is visible, the one that indicates error or the triangle is at the bottom right but does not cover the arrow. Video: 2) When there seems to be an error, the folder also gets the warning, but in the example in the image above, it doesn't. I think we gave enough input and it's best to wait for feedback from the maintainers here. I'm also happy to pair program on this PR if the Zed team thinks it makes sense (I read in the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pair-programming) that you sometimes do this).

If you can solve what I said in the previous comment it would be great.

Hey, i've just created a continuation PR for the git symbols in the project panel (and editor tabs), might want to check it out: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/20134

My two cents on the design here, is adding the existing error/warning icons to the end slot, where error takes precedence over warning, these icons should be additional to the git symbols i'm adding i.e not to replace them, they could be on the left of U/M/C.

For coloring, red for error and yellow for warning could take precedence over the git coloring, as the entries will have their respective git symbols if my PR gets merged. Project diagnostics overall sounds to me should have higher priority, i think this is how VSCode and Xcode also does it.

This would go in hand with the changes i've done in my PR that i mentioned.
this PR removed git coloring for icons in the project panel? 🤔

@danilo-leal i see, i know this is just an initial implementation but i think there are some things that can be cleared up, im trying to think from the average users perspective, but y'all know the best :>

if i were new, and the project panel showed me warning and error indicators on the file icon for diagnostics, and the file name was yellow (modified) or red (conflict) for git, and i solved the warning/error diagnostic problem but the filename is still colored yellow/red (for git) would confuse me, and vice versa if i solved a git problem and the yellow/red filename color went away while the warning/error indicator for diagnostics persisted. what's even more confusing now is that diagnostics coloring and git coloring for filenames take mixed priority, error diagnostics take highest priority, git takes second priority than warning diagnostics, and i know this because i've followed through the development of this but will the regular user know this?

if this is the path that is wanted, then maybe it would be better to either pick diagnostics or git (not both) for coloring? so i'd imagine with coloring mode to be set to diagnostics, it would color filenames either red or yellow, with no conflicting git colors, and git symbols (when/if merged) will be used to infer git information. or the opposite, that git coloring is enabled and you'd only infer diagnostics from the indicators (but the problem here is that the indicators are colored and small, so it still may not be clear to the user what it's actually for). i would personally recommend the former.

this is pushing me back on my git aware implementations for project panel entries and editor tabs, and i don't know what the vision/plan is here.

@nervenes I just pushed a PR earlier today that I think goes along your latter suggestion https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/20600. I hear you about the icons being potentially not clear, though. I guess we could solve it via a tooltip. Like, if you hover the file with the X error icon, you could see something like "There's an error" or a better label.

additionally, maybe clicking on the tooltip could take you to the particular error/warning in the diagnostic panel? also, is there any other place i could have a discussion with you, maybe any of the channels in the discord channel? i'd like to ask some questions about the git symbols, or should i open up an empty pr (that i'll later use for the implementation)?

@danilo-leal @nervenes Why not strike-through the filename for a git removal and use a darker red color if you need a color indicator? That way it very clearly separates it from diagnostics red, while adding a visual cue that a file was removed. This would accomplish the separation of functionality you are looking for while making the UX much nicer and explicit.

@hawkinsonb curious to explore that, yeah. Thanks for the suggestion!

issue_context.title: Show errors/warning counts in tree view
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the feature

In VS Code, I rely a lot on the explorer showing me in which files the compiler has found errors/warnings. Ideally, it would both use colors and a number of errors/warnings to indicate how badly my current state is broken.

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature


_No response_
comments: I know you are dealing with an enormous amount of requests/Issues and I really appreciate your work! I wanted to ask if this Issue is somewhere on the roadmap? This is something that would make my DX significantly better. I am going all-in on Zed but this is something I miss from VSCode.

FWIW, this seemed to be one of the most popular replies in this recent Twitter thread:

https://twitter.com/thorstenball/status/1772196113128272116
Yes this would be a fantastic add.
I would greatly benefit from this feature

Same here, our toolchain creates and modify files automatically, sometimes it's hard to know we have an issue before compile time. I'm absolutely in love with Zed and it's the last remaining feature that would make zed my daily driver !

Same issue, the only two missing parts for me are the source control tab and this one. I'm fine not having the source control tab any time soon, but not seeing errored files in the tree view and in the opened tabs list doesn't allow me to switch to Zed today.
If that could help, Zed has an outline view which can be opened for any [multi] buffer. There's no coloring, but if you open a diagnostics multi buffer it will show all files with errors in a tree:

> If that could help, Zed has an outline view which can be opened for any [multi] buffer. > > There's no coloring, but if you open a diagnostics multi buffer it will show all files with errors in a tree: This is definitely helpful, but just like a file is yellow if it has a change in it... having it red is immensely helpful. I don't have the screen real-estate to keep this window open -- love Zed, but this is the thing I miss most about vscode
Any update on this? Or even an alpha/beta build we can use to have this feature early?
This feature is the only deal-breaker for switching to Zed...
Agreed, with large monorepos this is essential.
tried to edit bevy in zed, it was not an optimal experience. it also doesn't work well with my VST
Would still benefit from an error lens implementation

review_comments: @mrnugget I went for a tuple to avoid chaining HashMaps if that is ok for you?

Yeah, our thinking was to color the text only when it's an error case; otherwise, the git-status has priority. This could help the confusion around the warning and modified colors because, in this case, there could be a warning in `foobar.rs` even if you haven't touched that file specifically.

Does this make sense? Open to feedback.
Yes sounds good :) Thank you so much @danilo-leal, the design looks fantastic!
